messages.author: 2af21328dc3f2578
messages.subject: transposing data?
parts:
Since this went so well last time...new question!

I'm trying to make a wide df from a long one, and I've been reading through the Specter chapters, trying all sorts of things, and can't seem to do what I want to do. 

Here's the head of the df:

   PlotID Species.Code X.Cover
1 A-1-001       CASSPP     0.5
2 A-1-001        LOTSP     0.5
3 A-1-001        ARTTRI     0.5
4 A-1-001       ERIWRI     0.5
5 A-1-001       ERICON     0.5
6 A-1-001       PINJEF    15.0

I have 113 more plots, each with a different number of species that each have their own observation of percent cover. I would like to end up with a df that has one row for each plot, one column for each spp, and the X.Cover (%cover) values in the appropriate cells. 0s or NAs are fine for plots where a spp doesn't occur. 

Each species (there are 337) is not listed for each plot, so there are no 0s already, if that matters. 

I've tried various table(), melt(), cast(), unstack(), and some reshape(), but I still can't figure out how to do what I want to do. Any ideas?

Thanks!

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: transposing data?
parts:
Here’s an alternative solution using tidyr, Hadley Wickham’s new successor to the reshape2 package:

library(tidyr)
df_long = data.frame(plot=rep(1:3, each=3), species=rep(letters[1:3], 3), 
                cover=runif(9))

df_long
df_wide = spread(df_long, species, cover)
df_wide

spread "spreads out" the species column into separate columns by value.

​

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: transposing data?
parts:
This implies that there are duplicate observations. That is, the same value for both plot and species in multiple rows. The error means that, since you have not specified what to do with duplicate values, dcast defaults to counting the number of observations. Look for any cells in the output that are 2 or greater - this should point you to the duplicate rows. If you want to sum or average duplicate rows, add the argument fun.aggregate=sum or fun.aggregate=mean to the dcast function call.

​

On Sat, Sep 6, 2014 at 11:21 AM, Mila Dunbar-Irwin <mila.hic...@gmail.com> wrote:
Actually, dcast is only working on a small subset of the entire dataset, but when I try to run it on the whole thing I get an error: "aggregation function missing: defaulting to length" and I get an output that's just in table format again (i.e. a 1 for a positive observation, not a value from X.Cover).

Any idea why that might be?
